title: The Reasoner pilot and the in-language MFQ-2 study: eleven language models on a moral-judgment instrument and on a moral-foundations questionnaire, with the runs, the scoring and analysis code, the human responses and the interactive viewers
description:
Repository snapshot for two exploratory documents, published together.

Eleven Language Models in a Narrow Band of a Moral-Judgment Instrument (papers/reasoner-pilot.md, .pdf; statistical appendix papers/reasoner-appendix.md, .pdf): the Reasoner instrument scores humans and language models on the same four bipolar axes from constant-sum allocations over a judgment question and a reasoning question per scenario. Eleven models from nine labs under eight framings on 48 scenarios, against 68 human respondents on twelve baseline scenarios.

Eleven language models take the MFQ-2 in English and six translations, with and without a country to answer as (papers/inlanguage-mfq2-DRAFT.md, .pdf): the same panel on the MFQ-2 in English and six official translations, framed as a typical person from each of twenty-three countries and unframed, against published human means for twenty countries.

The snapshot holds every collected run, the scoring function, the analysis scripts that regenerate every published number (python3 analysis/test_reproduce.py, no keys, no network), the anonymised human responses under CC BY 4.0, the two interactive viewers, the decision log and the adjudicated review records. Nothing here was preregistered; both documents say so. Software under Apache-2.0; data, figures and documents under CC BY 4.0 (DATA-LICENSE.md).
